<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. IX.|ACCORDING TO S. MARKE.|111}}</noinclude>said, O incredulous generation, hovv long shal I be vvith you? hovv long shal I suffer you? bring him vnto me. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=20}}† And they brought him. And vvhen he had seen him, immediatly the spirit troubled him: and being throvven vpon the ground, he tumbled foming. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=21}}† And he asked his father, Hovv long time is it since this hath chaunced vnto him? But he said, From his infancie: {{verse|chapter=9|verse=22}}† and often times hath he cast him into fire and into vvaters, to destroy him. but if thou canst any thing, helpe vs, hauing compassion on vs. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=23}}† And Iesus said to him, If thou canst beleeue, al things are possible to him that beleeueth. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=24}}† And incontinent the father of the boy crying out, vvith teares said, I do beleeue Lord: helpe my incredulity. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=25}}† And vvhen {{sc|Iesvs}} savv the people running together, he threatened the vncleane spirit, saying to him, Deafe and dumme spirit, I commaunde thee, goe out of him, and enter not any more into him. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=26}}† And crying out, and greatly tearing him, he vvent out of him, and he became as dead, so that many said, That he is dead. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=27}}† But {{sc|Iesvs}} holding his hand, lifted him vp: and he rose. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=28}}† And vvhen he vvas entred into the house, his Disciples secretely asked him, Why could not vve cast him out? {{verse|chapter=9|verse=29}}† And he said to them, This kinde can goe out by nothing, but {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Note the great force of prayer, and fasting.}}∷ by prayer and fasting.⊣

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=30}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 17, 22. Lu. 9, 21.''}}* departing thence they passed by Galilee, neither vvould he that any man should knovv. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=31}}† And he taught his Disciples, and said to them, That the Sonne of man shal be betrayed into the hands of men, and they shal kil him, and being killed the third day he shal rise againe. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=32}}† But they knevv not the vvord: and they vvere afraid to aske him.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=33}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 18, 1. Lu. 9, 46.''}}* they came to Capharnaum. VVho, vvhen he vvas in the house, asked them, What did you treate of in the vvay? {{verse|chapter=9|verse=34}}† But they held their peace. for in the vvay they had disputed among them selues, vvhich of them should be the greater. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=35}}† And sitting dovvne, he called the Tvvelue, and saith to them, If any man vvil be first, he shal be last of al, and the minister of al. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=36}}† And taking a childe, he set him in the middes of them. VVhom vvhen he had embraced, he said to them, {{verse|chapter=9|verse=37}}† VVhosoeuer shal receiue one of such children in my name, receiueth me. and vvhosoeuer shal receiue me, receiueth not me, but him that sent me.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=38}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Lu. 9, 49.''}}* Iohn ansvvered him, saying, Maister vve savv one casting out deuils {{sup|‖}} in thy name, vvho folovveth not vs, and vve<noinclude>{{rh|||prohibited}}</noinclude>
